title: 1968 AHSME Problem 10
statement:
Assume that, for a certain school, it is true that

\(\mathrm{I}:\) Some students are not honest.

\(\mathrm{II}:\) All fraternity members are honest.

A necessary conclusion is:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: Some fraternity members are not students

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: Some students are not fraternity members

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: No fraternity member is a student

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: No student is a fraternity member

solutions.text:
Statement \(\mathrm{I}\) guarantees a dishonest student. Statement \(\mathrm{II}\) says every fraternity member is honest, so that dishonest student cannot be a fraternity member. Hence some student is not a fraternity member.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Choose a student whose existence is guaranteed by statement \(\mathrm{I}\)
Could that dishonest student be a fraternity member under statement \(\mathrm{II}?\)
